hook: In May 2026, researchers turned pure silk threads into transparent plastic.

sections.voiceover: In May 2026, researchers turned pure silk threads into transparent plastic.
sections.visual_cue: Macro shot of raw silkworm silk thread transforming under pressure into a clear glass-like polymer sheet.
sections.sfx_cue: Low metallic hum rising to a crisp snap

sections.voiceover: Engineers at University of Michigan fused silk threads under high heat. Where will 3 labs guide 6G light waves?
sections.visual_cue: Split screen showing university laboratory presses fusing silk fibers, followed by a map highlighting Michigan, London, and Tufts.
sections.sfx_cue: Pneumatic press hiss followed by subtle digital ping
b_roll: University of Michigan engineering lab high pressure press
Imperial College London materials testing apparatus

sections.voiceover: However, Nature Sustainability showed that silk threads didn't process easily into strong materials for telecom applications.
sections.visual_cue: Diagram of fragile fibroin protein chain fracturing under high-frequency electromagnetic radiation.
b_roll: Microscopic fibroin protein structure breakdown diagram

sections.voiceover: Published in Nature Sustainability, 3 universities transformed silkworm silk into solid components. The 2026 design cuts chemical waste while preserving thread strength.
sections.visual_cue: 3D render of terahertz light beam spiraling through fused silk component into a 6G signal tower receiver.
b_roll: 6G transmitter component prototype with laser beam passing through

sections.voiceover: Silkworm threads now power next generation 6G network hardware.
sections.visual_cue: Extreme close-up of finished silk telecom component installed inside modern 6G antenna housing.
sections.sfx_cue: Deep bass tone settling into silence
b_roll: Next generation 6G telecom circuit board with transparent silk optic element
